body.x: KEISER Inc. (CEO DuHeon Gyeon) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9, as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

Keiser is a label and content platform that enables music search and recommendations through a Genre Component Combination (GCC) search engine and allows released music to be used, settled, and traded without copyright concerns. It is a cultural content tech company that has begun global expansion based on an integrated copyright system, AI, and blockchain technologies designed for the present and future era in which the boundaries between creators and users continue to blur.

The company launched its platform service this year and secured TIPS investment backed by KVIC. It currently holds 11 certifications, including GS Level 1 and copyright-safety certification, has received 17 awards, such as CES Innovation Awards and ministerial commendations, and owns 12 patents, including three registered in the United States.

Keiser has built its initial infrastructure by contracting with 500 musicians and releasing more than 1,000 music tracks. It has also completed system preparations for contracting with overseas local artists and releasing music internationally. All music released by Keiser is available on major domestic and global music platforms, while its proprietary music platform, JIGPU, allows users to use music without copyright concerns. In addition, the company has signed agreements to integrate its GCC search technology and JIGPU with AI mental care solution and app service companies.

At CES 2026, Keiser plans to introduce JIGPU, a copyright-focused content platform equipped with the GCC engine. The platform is specialized for music users, including video, game, metaverse, and broadcast creators, as well as for music producers, such as musicians and agencies. It enables content creators to search for music by defining their needs in terms of objective musical characteristics and to freely use high-quality released music found on the platform without copyright concerns. Other key features include an integrated blockchain system for copyright and ownership management, covering copyright management, transactions, and investments, as well as built-in music release functions that enable artist contracting, music distribution, and settlement without intermediaries.
Keiser continues to expand its artist network across Korea, the United States, Vietnam, and Japan, and plans to use CES 2026 as the launchpad for a full-scale overseas expansion.

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
